1.5.0 Release Notes

longbook is a memory for your financial commitments, on iPhone and Mac. This page lists what each version brings, newest first, starting with 1.4.1, the first release on the App Store.

The longbook team · 24 October 2026 · 6 min read

Feeling lazy to read? Ask your AI to summarise.

Read https://longbook.app/blog/release-notes.md and summarise it for me in 5 bullet points.

longbook keeps the payments that come back, such as subscriptions, insurance, rent and loans, in a folder in your own iCloud. Every new version is added to this page, so the newest one is always at the top.

1.5.0

Released on [release date] for iPhone and Mac. Getting started is shorter, a statement review shows everything on one list, Support is on every screen, and the Mac gets its own Settings window. Here is what it brings, grouped by what you do with longbook.

Getting started

  • Three steps. Welcome and sign in, activate your longbook, then import a statement. Once a statement is kept, your longbook opens.
  • A place to start. If you skip the statement, the Dashboard offers three ways in: import a statement, add a commitment by hand, or use your own AI. On the Mac, you can also drop a statement file on it.
  • A tutorial for each screen. The first time you open a screen, a short tutorial shows what it is for. Replay any of them in Settings, then Tutorials.
  • Family Sharing, on its own card. The purchase screen shows that everyone in your Apple family gets longbook on their own account and devices.
  • What changed, after an update. What's New shows the changes once after an update. Open it again from Settings, or read every version on this page.

Importing a statement

  • One list to review. The review shows Commitments, Past expenses, People and Accounts, in that order, with every item ticked. Untick what is wrong and tap Add. The review closes and Proposals shows what was recorded.
  • Nothing it prints is missed. The review offers every person and every account the statement prints, your own other accounts included, along with the accounts and people your transfers and card payments go to. The statement's own account is always named, even when its header prints no number.
  • Your choice. Adding a statement's people and accounts can be turned off in Settings.
  • Optimize your data. The setup questions moved to Settings. The people and accounts you pick there are hints that help longbook read your statements, and they are not added to People and Accounts.

Every day

  • Changes is now Proposals. The screen that holds what you or your AI added is called Proposals, so it no longer reads like Charges at a glance.
  • This charge, or every one after it. Deleting a planned charge asks whether to remove only that one, or that one and every one after it, which also ends the commitment's plan there.
  • Stars, search and filters. Star a person or an account to keep it at the top of its list. People and Accounts each have a search and a filter by relationship or type.
  • Examples from your region. Naming a new account shows an example from your region, and the UPI account type is offered in India only. Accounts that already have that type keep it.
  • Open another longbook. Settings, then Data & privacy, can open a longbook from another folder, and leaves your current folder as it is.

Support

  • Help on every screen. A Support button sits in the corner of every screen on iPhone and Mac, and steps aside while Support is open.
  • Ask, or write to a person. Ask a question and longbook's AI answers from the help articles, or email the team.
  • Show us the screen. The camera button attaches a screenshot of your screen to your message, and longbook's AI reads it to help. A screenshot can show amounts, so check it before you send it.

Your AI

  • Use My Own AI. It copies a prompt that sets longbook up for you: in Claude, the longbook plugin or connector, and in ChatGPT, a plugin named longbook with its website and icon.
  • It reads the guide first. An AI connected to longbook reads longbook's guide for the task before it writes, and is told which part to read when it has not.
  • Every choice, on the Mac. An AI connected to longbook on your Mac sees every choice its tools offer, such as listing cancelled commitments or reading one chapter of the guide.

On the Mac

  • A real Settings window. Settings in the sidebar opens a menu, and Settings opens the Settings window, with panes for General, Appearance, Account, AI, Statements, Data & privacy, Tutorials and About.
  • Open at login. longbook can open at login, check for updates on its own, and hide its Dock icon while the menu bar shows the next payment.
  • A shorter sidebar. The sidebar shows only the people and accounts you star.
  • Controls that answer the pointer. Buttons, sidebar rows and cards light up under the pointer and darken while pressed. Tab shows a focus ring, and controls you cannot use yet are dimmed.
  • Buttons for iCloud and backups. Move to iCloud and Back Up Now in Settings are buttons.
  • A steadier start. longbook no longer quits at launch while it reads a crash report from an earlier session.

On longbook.app

  • Pages your AI can read. When an AI assistant asks longbook.app for Markdown, it gets each page's text without the layout, and AI tools can find the longbook server's details on the site.
  • Pictures you may use. The blog's pictures now say how you may use them, the same way as the media kit: free for writing about longbook.

1.4.1

Released 24 October 2026 for iPhone and Mac. This is the first version of longbook on the App Store. Here is what it brings, grouped by what you do with longbook.

Getting started

  • A clear way in. Two welcome pages, each with Back, then Sign in with Apple, then Activate your longbook, which leads with the 7-day refund.
  • Buy it, then use it. An account without a licence opens on the purchase screen, with Restore Purchase and a demo to look around first.
  • 12 months of Cloud, and a refund. A licence includes 12 months of longbook Cloud. In Account, Request a Refund is there for 7 days after you buy.
  • Your longbook without iCloud. If you would rather not use iCloud, longbook can keep your longbook on this iPhone instead. By default it stays in your own iCloud.

Importing a statement

  • A review that looks like Changes. Importing a statement shows what was read, with Discard and Add at the top, then the charges, people and repeats one tab at a time. It is the same layout as Changes.
  • Repeating payments become commitments. The repeating payments you tick when reading a statement become commitments, planned ahead, so Coming up fills from the first statement.
  • Any currency. A statement in pounds, dollars or any other currency is read in that currency, not rupees.
  • Kept straight away. A statement you import is kept at once and filed in History, so Changes does not ask again.
  • Your say before it goes to an AI. Before longbook first sends a statement to an AI, it asks you to accept the privacy policy, with the policy right there to read. What happens to the statement after that is in how longbook turns your bank statements into data.

Every day

  • Light, Dark or Automatic, at once. On iPhone, the appearance you pick takes effect straight away, without restarting the app.
  • Search by what the card says. Search finds commitments by what their cards say: Cancelling, Free trial, Yearly, Paid and more.
  • One kind of list. Relationship and account type get the same search-or-add list as category.
  • Nothing to review. When nothing is waiting, Changes says Nothing to review, with a way into History.
  • Large text. At the largest text sizes, screens rearrange so every word reads in full.

On the Mac

  • Sheets open in the middle of the window. Sheets, and Sign in with Apple, open centred in the window.
  • Rows that name no one. Accounts and People also show the rows that name no one.
  • The timeline reaches further. Pull the timeline past its end to reveal the button that switches to the next or last 30 payments.

Your account

  • Deleting says what goes and what stays. Before your account is deleted, longbook says what goes and what stays, offers to save a copy of your longbook first, and asks you to type DELETE. An account opened with Apple ends its Apple link too.

Download longbook for iPhone and Mac. If something here does not match what you see, write to us.

About longbook

longbook is a memory for your financial commitments: subscriptions, insurance, rent, loans and every other payment that comes back. It runs on iPhone and Mac and keeps its records as plain files in your own iCloud.

The next payment stays in view on the iPhone widget and in the Mac menu bar. Your AI can read your longbook and update it through longbook's MCP server, and every change it makes shows in Proposals, to keep or undo.
